title: LumaScale evaluation kickoff - security, compliance, and load acceptance
topics: security & compliance: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs
timeline for 4-week evaluation and pilot handoff
summary: Kickoff for a 4-week evaluation of Redwood inference for LumaScale's document-summarization service. Team covered acceptance criteria (P95 latency, token cost thresholds, embedding recall), benchmarking plan (synthetic replay + production shadow traffic), workload sizing (avg seq length, concurrency), and security/compliance checkpoints (SOC 2 evidence, ISO, Okta SAML for SSO, RBAC roles, audit log retention and export). Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, access for IDP test tenant, schedule week-by-week benchmarks, and provide SOC 2 + ISO artifacts.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood), Sara Lopez (LumaScale CTO), Marcus Reid (Eng Lead), Priya Nair (Security PM), Omar Haddad (SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is maya from redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with david and lena from our eng team. sara, marcus, priya, omar — thanks for making time.
[00:18] Sara Lopez: hey thanks, yeah excited to get into this. we want to validate performance for our summarization pipeline and lock down the security checklist for a short eval.
[00:30] David Ortiz: quick agenda — success criteria, workload profile, benchmark plan, security/compliance asks, and timeline. any additions?
[00:37] Marcus Reid: maybe also fallback model behavior and how caching affects latency numbers.
[00:45] David Ortiz: good, we'll cover model variants and caching (key-V cache) notes. 
[01:05] Priya Nair: on security we specifically need SOC 2 type 2 evidence, ISO 27001 cert if available, SSO with our Okta tenant via SAML, audit log export and retention policy, and role-based access controls for developer/ops/audit roles.
[01:28] Maya Chen: understood. we have SOC 2 artifacts and ISO summary — we'll share those. SAML SSO flows we've done with several customers; we can provide a test IdP config and a temporary tenant for integration. audit logs are available via our console and can be exported; retention is configurable.
[01:48] Omar Haddad: retention — what's the default window? we often have a 12 month requirement, with the ability to export to our SIEM.
[01:55] Lena Park: default is 90 days in the console, but we support archival export to S3 for longer retention. we can set up a push to your SIEM during the eval.
[02:10] Marcus Reid: great. for workload: our summarizer receives ~120 reqs/sec at peak, average sequence length is around 800 tokens input, output avg 120 tokens. 80% of requests in EU region.
[02:30] David Ortiz: ok that maps to about X tokens/sec, we'll translate to GPU capacity. do you expect bursts?
[02:38] Sara Lopez: bursts up to 300 rps for short 10–15 minute windows when big imports finish.
[02:45] David Ortiz: noted. success criteria proposal: P95 latency < 220ms for single-turn summarization on our hosted inference with model X-3 small quant, throughput sustaining 150 rps with <5% error rate, embedding recall for rerank above 0.88 on your sample eval set, and token-cost per doc below $0.015 — are those realistic targets?
[03:10] Marcus Reid: P95 at 220ms sounds optimistic given our sequences, is that measured end-to-end or just inference?
[03:18] Maya Chen: that was inference-only. end-to-end we should budget extra for network and client-side processing; we'll document both.
[03:27] Priya Nair: on compliance gate — we need proof of data residency controls for EU requests, and confirmation that logs and artifacts for the eval won't include raw PII.
[03:40] Lena Park: during the eval we can mask PII in logs and use a synthetic dataset reflection of your workload; we can also pin region to eu-west-1 for the pilot.
[03:54] Marcus Reid: benchmarking approach?
[03:58] David Ortiz: two-track: 1) synthetic replay using a recorded request trace you provide (sanitized), driving concurrency matrixes; 2) shadowing — route a subset of production traffic in read-only mode to Redwood Hosted, comparing latency and outputs. we'll run multiple model variants and cache configurations.
[04:22] Sara Lopez: for the synthetic replay we'll need a template of the trace format, and the spreadsheet for results.
[04:28] Maya Chen: we'll send a benchmark spreadsheet with columns for model variant, batch size, sequence length buckets, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error count, and token cost.
[04:41] Omar Haddad: how do you simulate KV cache hits? our production has a warm cache for repeated doc edits.
[04:49] David Ortiz: we have options — either replay with prefixes that match your cache warming pattern or inject a separate cache-hit simulation; we'll coordinate with your SRE.
[05:05] Marcus Reid: winning acceptance criteria includes quality checks — we can't sacrifice summary coherence. how will that be measured?
[05:12] Lena Park: we'll run a small eval harness with your labeled prompt sets and compute ROUGE/F1 and a human spot-check. if quality regresses by more than X%, we flag it.
[05:24] Sara Lopez: what's X%?
[05:26] David Ortiz: we normally use 3–5% tolerance depending on metric; propose 4% for this eval.
[05:32] Priya Nair: back to security — RBAC: can we have separate roles for admin, ops, developer, and an auditor with read-only access to logs? Also MFA enforced for admin.
[05:44] Maya Chen: yes — RBAC supports custom roles. MFA is supported for console access; for SSO we expect Okta to enforce MFA.
[05:52] Priya Nair: good. audit logs — do they include request payloads? we prefer metadata only, with payload redaction.
[05:59] Lena Park: full payloads are optional; for your tenancy we can enable payload redaction by default and provide hashes for traceability.
[06:12] Omar Haddad: about KMS — we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys.
[06:18] Maya Chen: BYOK with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys via HSM is supported on Private deployments. For hosted we provide envelope encryption with KMS; we can discuss a dedicated key for the eval if needed.
[06:33] Marcus Reid: that implies Private deployment. are we expected to run Private for the short eval?
[06:39] David Ortiz: not necessarily. we can do hosted with stricter controls (region pinning, redaction, SIEM export) for the eval. if you require BYOK/HSM, that pushes to Dedicated/Private. we'll map the path depending on the security gate severity.
[06:55] Sara Lopez: timeline — we're aiming to decide vendor in 6 weeks; the eval needs to finish and present results by week 4. is a 4-week schedule realistic?
[07:04] Maya Chen: yes, typical 4-week eval: week 0 (kickoff and access), week 1 (integration + smoke tests), week 2 (synthetic benchmarks), week 3 (shadow + regression checks), week 4 (analysis + acceptance).
[07:18] David Ortiz: we'll provide a detailed runbook and a calendar for test windows.
[07:25] Marcus Reid: test windows — we need them outside of our peak import times; we'll provide preferred windows.
[07:32] Priya Nair: evidence package for security — what exactly will you share?
[07:37] Maya Chen: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), ISO summary/certificate if available, penetration test summary, list of sub-processors, data flow diagrams, and an SOC 2 bridge letter addressing control gaps.
[07:51] Priya Nair: who signs the bridge letter?
[07:54] Maya Chen: our security lead will sign; david can follow up with contacts.
[08:00] David Ortiz: ok on benchmarking specifics — can you confirm sample sizes for quality tests? how many labeled docs do you have?
[08:07] Sara Lopez: about 4k labeled summaries across various doc lengths; we can provide a stratified sample of 500 for automated runs and another 50-100 for manual review.
[08:19] David Ortiz: that's ideal. for throughput tests we'll request a 20k request trace sanitized for replay.
[08:27] Marcus Reid: latency targets again — inference-only P95 <220ms was the ask, but given seq lengths I'm concerned. can we fallback to a slightly larger latency SLO for initial runs?
[08:37] Maya Chen: yes propose a stepped SLO: week2 target P95 <300ms to tune caching and instance sizing, week3 target P95 <240ms with optimized batching, and final acceptance at <220ms if quality holds.
[08:55] Priya Nair: will you provide per-token cost estimates per model variant? we need cost-per-summary estimations.
[09:01] Lena Park: yes that will be in the benchmark sheet; we'll include model footprints and tokenized counts across buckets.
[09:08] Sara Lopez: can we do a dedicated canary with a tiny subset in week3?
[09:12] David Ortiz: yes — week3 shadowing + canary with 1% live traffic is possible if you give the routing rules.
[09:20] Omar Haddad: from infra perspective we'll need network allowlists and IP ranges for your hosted endpoints.
[09:26] Maya Chen: will provide IP ranges and a VPN option if needed.
[09:30] Marcus Reid: QA — how do we validate the embedding recall metric? are you running nearest neighbor exact matches to our golden set?
[09:37] Lena Park: we'll compute embedding vectors and evaluate recall@k over your labeled rerank tasks and compare against your current system.
[09:45] Priya Nair: any questions on contractual constraints? we have DPA terms and need to confirm data processing addendum aligns.
[09:52] Maya Chen: our DPA template includes subprocessors and retention and should be fine; legal can run a quick pass during the eval.
[09:59] Sara Lopez: ok — anything about regulatory or ISO audit detail we should clarify now?
[10:04] David Ortiz: only that ISO 27001 certificate may be in process — we can share the current evidence pack.
[10:10] Maya Chen: now to action items and next steps — we'll capture specifics.
[10:14] [Roundtable — clarifications and quick questions]
[45:00] Maya Chen: (closing) recap — redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2/ISO artifacts, SAML test config, and a runbook for week-by-week tasks. LumaScale to send sanitized replay trace, labeled sample set, preferred test windows, and Okta test tenant access. we'll aim to lock calendar slots for week1 smoke and week2 benchmark runs.
[45:30] Sara Lopez: sounds good. we'll try to get the sanitized trace by EOD Friday and set up the Okta test tenant early next week.
[46:00] David Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up with invite updates and the artifact links.
[46:12] Meeting end.
